name: Patagonia
description: Pioneer of environmental activism in outdoor apparel. Donates 1% of sales to environmental causes, uses regenerative organic agriculture, and runs the Worn Wear repair & resale program. In 2022, founder Yvon Chouinard transferred ownership to a climate trust.
certifications: B Corp, Fair Trade, Bluesign, GOTS
keyPractices: 1% for the Planet, Fair Trade Certified, regenerative organic agriculture, Worn Wear program

name: Adidas
description: Sportswear giant making moves on sustainability via its Parley ocean plastic programme and a shift towards recycled polyester. Campus respondents rated it higher than its Good On You score, possibly due to brand familiarity and visible sustainability marketing.
keyPractices: Parley ocean plastic, moving towards recycled polyester, some sustainability commitments

name: Nike
description: Nike's Move to Zero campaign pledges carbon and waste reduction, and it uses some recycled materials. However, labour concerns persist in its global supply chain. Campus respondents scored it near Adidas, reflecting brand recognition over verified ethics.
keyPractices: Move to Zero campaign, some sustainable materials, labor concerns in supply chain

name: Levi's
description: Levi's Water<Less manufacturing technique has saved over 3 billion litres of water since 2011. While they've made improvements on environmental front, supply chain transparency and labour practices still lag behind best-in-class brands.
keyPractices: Water<Less technique, F.L.X. customization, some sustainable collections

name: The North Face
description: The North Face holds Responsible Down Standard and Bluesign certifications and has committed to circular design. However, as part of VF Corporation, it lags behind leaders like Patagonia in verified environmental commitments.
keyPractices: Responsible Down Standard, some recycled materials, circular design initiatives

name: Uniqlo
description: Uniqlo produces high-quality basics and has made some commitments to sustainable materials, but remains limited in supply chain transparency. Its LifeWear philosophy promotes longevity over trends, which is a positive signal.
keyPractices: Some sustainable materials, limited transparency on supply chain

name: Zara
description: Zara's Join Life eco-collection uses some sustainable materials, but it remains one of the world's largest fast fashion operations producing hundreds of millions of garments per year. Campus respondents gave it similar scores to H&M.
keyPractices: Join Life collection, some eco materials, but still fast fashion model

name: H&M
description: H&M's Conscious Collection was the subject of multiple greenwashing investigations across Europe. Despite a garment collecting programme, its fast fashion model and overproduction remain core concerns. Campus gave it the lowest score among all surveyed brands.
keyPractices: Conscious collection, garment collecting program, but greenwashing concerns

name: Puma
description: Puma's FOREVER BETTER sustainability programme covers materials, water use, and worker welfare. Campus respondents gave it a 4.0, on par with Nike and Adidas, suggesting brand perception outpaces independently verified progress.
keyPractices: Some sustainability initiatives, FOREVER BETTER program

name: Lululemon
description: Despite premium pricing, Lululemon rates 'Not Good Enough' on Good On You. It has set some sustainability goals but lacks the transparency and verified certifications expected of a brand at its price point. Campus respondents gave it a below-average 3.42.
keyPractices: Some sustainability goals, but lacks transparency

name: Gap
description: Gap has some sustainable programmes but applies them inconsistently across its portfolio. Good On You rates it 'Not Good Enough', while campus respondents gave a surprisingly moderate 3.88 — likely reflecting familiarity over knowledge of its practices.
keyPractices: Some sustainable programs, but inconsistent

name: Massimo Dutti
description: Massimo Dutti uses a medium proportion of lower-impact materials but lacks transparency on sustainability goals. As an Inditex brand (same parent as Zara), it carries the same structural concerns around fast fashion overproduction.
keyPractices: Medium proportion lower-impact materials, lacks transparency on goals

name: Forever 21
description: Forever 21 has no verifiable environmental measures and publishes no public data on its practices. Good On You rates it 'We Avoid' — the lowest possible rating. A flagship example of the worst that fast fashion has to offer.
keyPractices: No verifiable environmental measures, no public data

name: non.
description: A niche denim brand committed to raw selvedge denim and living wages for all final-stage workers. Radical transparency on wages and working conditions make it a standout in an industry notorious for exploitation.
keyPractices: Raw selvedge-denim, living wages for final stage workers

name: Infantium Victoria
description: GOTS certified and PETA-vegan certified childrenswear brand applying circular economy principles. One of the few fashion brands to hold both organic and vegan certification simultaneously.
keyPractices: GOTS certified, PETA-vegan certified, circular principles

name: Automic Gold
description: Queer-owned jewelry brand using reclaimed materials with full living wage transparency. A rare combination of ethical production, minority ownership, and radical openness about pay practices in a sector where exploitation is common.
keyPractices: Reclaimed materials, queer-owned, living wage transparency

name: Rifò
description: Italian circular fashion brand using centuries-old textile recycling traditions from Prato. Publishes full supplier lists and builds its entire model around circular economy principles.
keyPractices: Circular economy, supplier lists, centuries-old recycling methods

name: TERAS
description: A handcrafted brand employing disadvantaged workers and reviving traditional Japanese sashiko and boro textile crafts. Combines meaningful employment with sustainable, repair-based fashion philosophy.
keyPractices: Employs disadvantaged workers, sashiko and boro crafts

name: soleRebels
description: Ethiopian footwear brand making shoes from recycled car tyres and paying workers 3× the local industry average. A globally recognised model of ethical production from a developing nation.
keyPractices: Ethiopian recycled tyre shoes, wages 3x industry average

name: GuterStoff
description: Certified organic, vegan, and fairly made since 2008 — a veteran of ethical fashion long before it became mainstream. Consistent standards across its entire basics range with full third-party certification.
keyPractices: Certified organic, vegan, fairly made since 2008

name: ReCreate
description: A boutique brand focused on fair employment, training, and worker empowerment. Goes beyond paying fair wages to actively invest in worker development and community empowerment programmes.
keyPractices: Fair employment, training, empowerment focus

name: ESSĒN
description: Uses limited production runs and low-waste cutting techniques to minimise both overproduction and fabric waste. A principled slow-fashion approach to accessories.
keyPractices: Limited production runs, low-waste cutting techniques

name: Indilisi
description: Celebrates heritage weaving crafts and uses deadstock fabrics from factories that would otherwise waste them. Supports artisan communities while keeping textile waste out of landfill.
keyPractices: Heritage crafts, handweaving, deadstock fabrics

name: Akyn
description: Founded by a sustainability industry veteran, Akyn is built from the ground up on lower-impact materials and genuine ethical practice rather than retrofit marketing.
keyPractices: Lower impact materials, founded by sustainability legend

name: Agazi
description: Polish footwear brand making vegan shoes from innovative plant-based materials — hemp fabric, apple skin leather, and grape skin leather derived from winery byproducts. A leader in next-generation vegan footwear materials.
keyPractices: Vegan, hemp and apple skin/grape-based leathers

name: Kotn
description: B Corp certified brand working directly with Egyptian cotton farmers in the Nile Delta and funding school construction in farming communities. Combines supply chain transparency with meaningful community development.
keyPractices: B Corp, supports education in Nile Delta communities

name: Armedangels
description: German brand using GOTS certified organic cotton and a member of Fair Wear Foundation. A solid all-rounder in ethical basics, known for modern design that doesn't sacrifice sustainability credentials.
keyPractices: GOTS cotton, Fair Wear Foundation member

name: ASKET
description: Swedish essentials brand with a radical 'permanent collection' — no seasonal drops, ever. Publishes transparent pricing breakdowns and eliminates middlemen. A model of principled anti-fashion.
keyPractices: Permanent collection, fair pricing, no middlemen

name: Dawn Denim
description: Sustainable denim brand with a genuine commitment to inclusive sizing from XS to 3XL — rare in sustainable fashion, which often defaults to limited size ranges. Combines environmental progress with body inclusivity.
keyPractices: Sustainable denim, inclusive sizing XS-3XL

name: OhSevenDays
description: Istanbul-based brand using deadstock fabrics from local factories that would otherwise be discarded. Keeps production and materials local, dramatically reducing transportation emissions while supporting local artisans.
keyPractices: Deadstock fabrics from Istanbul factories

name: NAE
description: Portuguese vegan footwear brand using recycled PET bottles, cork, and pineapple leaf fibre (Piñatex). A showcase of how innovative plant-based and recycled materials can replace animal leather entirely.
keyPractices: Vegan, recycled PET, cork, pineapple leaf fiber

name: ISTO.
description: Portuguese brand publishing true cost breakdowns for every garment — exactly how much materials, labour, shipping, and margin cost. A single annual collection model resists the pressure of seasonal overproduction.
keyPractices: Single collection, true cost transparency

name: LOVE BRAND & Co
description: UK swimwear brand using a high proportion of lower-impact materials. Combines conservation partnership ethos with ethical production — a more principled choice in a market dominated by virgin synthetic fabrics.
keyPractices: High proportion lower-impact materials

name: Vigo Swim
description: Puerto Rican swimwear brand using OEKO-TEX certified fabrics, ensuring no harmful substances in production. A standout in sustainable swimwear from an underrepresented region in ethical fashion.
keyPractices: OEKO-TEX certified fabrics

name: Smalls Merino
description: UK merino wool brand known for its transparency about wool supplier relationships. In a sector where animal welfare standards are often opaque, Smalls provides clear information about where and how its merino is sourced.
keyPractices: Transparent about supplier relationships

name: Caftanii
description: Italian resortwear brand using organic linen and cotton in partnership with local artisans. Preserves traditional Italian textile craftsmanship while ensuring certified organic material standards.
keyPractices: Organic linen and cotton, artisan partnerships

name: QWSTION
description: Swiss accessories brand using vegetable-tanned leather and low-waste cutting. Creator of Bananatex® — a material made from banana plant fibre — demonstrating innovation in sustainable textile development.
keyPractices: Vegetable-tanned leather, low-waste cutting

name: Modibodi
description: Australian period underwear brand paying living wages in its final production stage. The reusable nature of its products fundamentally reduces disposable period product waste — an environmental benefit that goes beyond supply chain standards.
keyPractices: Living wages in final production stage

name: Eco Intimates
description: Australian lingerie brand using organic cotton and offering genuine size inclusivity up to 4XL — exceptional in a sector known for narrow sizing. Combines certified materials with an inclusive brand mission.
keyPractices: Organic cotton, inclusive sizing up to 4XL

name: hernest project
description: Premium loungewear brand using lower-impact fabrics and embracing size inclusivity. Brings ethical credentials to the comfort category without the premium pricing typically associated with sustainable loungewear.
keyPractices: Premium lower-impact fabrics, inclusive sizing

name: Zudio
description: Indian value fashion brand mentioned in the campus survey by one respondent who gave it the highest possible score. Not yet independently rated by Good On You. Common in Indian student wardrobes due to affordability.
keyPractices: Value fashion brand mentioned in survey

name: Bata
description: Global footwear brand operating across 70+ countries, headquartered in Switzerland. Popular in South Asian markets. Campus respondent rated it 4/5 but the brand has not been independently assessed for ethical practices.
keyPractices: Traditional footwear brand

name: Westside
description: Indian department store brand (part of Tata Group) rated 5/5 by one campus respondent. Not independently assessed for ethical fashion practices. Tata Group's broader ESG commitments may influence perception.
keyPractices: Indian department store brand

name: Reebok
description: Classic sportswear brand (now owned by Authentic Brands Group after Adidas divested it in 2022). Has made some sustainability commitments including its Cotton + Corn collection. Not yet independently rated in this database.
keyPractices: Sportswear brand
